_description.summary: Control flow and program structure: evaluation and iteration (Hermes', Thoth's, Thetis', Arke's, Prometheus' gambits, map and reduce, for-range, Sisyphus, Aleph, FSM), conditionals (Helios', Selene's, Coalescing), call stacks (Hanoi), splinters, wisps (projectile and cyclic), gates, portals, casting cassettes, callbacks, wish, staff casting stack.
use_cases: Executing lists of patterns, including with jumps
Creating and controlling wisps, splinters, gates or portals

colorize.d: I must be holding a Pigment in my other hand to cast this spell. When I do, it will consume the dye and permanently change my mind's coloration (at least, until I cast the spell again). Costs about one Amethyst Dust.

cycle_variant.d: Certain items I create seem oddly receptive to the influence of media. By holding a Cypher, Trinket, Artifact, Focus, or Spellbook in my other hand, I can use this spell to change the appearance of the item. Costs a negligible amount of media.

eval.d: Remove something evaluatable (usually a pattern or an entire Hex) from the stack, then cast it as if I had drawn the relevant patterns with my Staff.

eval/cc.d: Cast something evaluatable from the stack exactly like Hermes' Gambit, except that a unique "Jump" iota is pushed to the stack beforehand.

for_each.d: Remove something evaluatable and a list from the stack, then cast the evaluatable over each element of the list.

eval/prompt.d: Cast a pattern or list of patterns from the stack exactly like Hermes' Gambit, except that anything outside of this cast will not be captured by an Arke's Gambit within it.

eval/prompt_at.d: Like Thetis' Gambit, but also sets the jump tag of the cast to the given iota. If the iota is Null, this is equivalent to Thetis' Gambit.

eval/control.d: Cast a pattern or list of patterns from the stack similarly to Iris' Gambit. Must be drawn within Thetis' Gambit.

eval/control_at.d: Like Arke's Gambit, but only patterns within an enclosing Thetis' Gambit II with a jump tag matching the given iota are captured. If the iota is Null, this is equivalent to Arke's Gambit.

eval/setup_goto.d: Cast a list of patterns from the stack exactly like Hermes' Gambit, except that a Prometheus' Gambit within this cast will jump to an index within this list of patterns.

eval/goto.d: Remove a number from the stack, then jump to that index in the list cast by the enclosing Elbrus' Gambit. If the number is negative, the index counts from the end of the list instead.

bubble.d: Pushes a Bubbled Iota, which when popped via execution (by Hermes' or the likes), will push the contained iota to the stack.

pure_map.d: Similar to Thoth's Gambit, but won't copy the original stack inside each sub-execution.

pure_reduce.d: Similar to Thoth's Gambit; for data list with length **n**, it executes **n - 1** times; The first initial stack is the first two elements, and each subsequent execution uses the stack after the last execution.

for_range/cube.d: Executes given list on each point as initial iota inside the cuboid defined by given 2 points as body diagonal.

for_range/cube/pure.d:
...and yes, there are pure version for those shaped mapping patterns, too.
Everything the same, except that original stack isn't copied into each sub-executions.

for_range/line.d: Executes given list on each point as initial iota on the line connecting 2 points (start, end).

for_range/line/pure.d: Everything the same, except that original stack isn't copied into each sub-executions.

inf_loop.d:
*(technically not a Thoth but...)*
Consumes and executes given executable on current stack **INFINITELY, UNTIL THE END.**

fsm.d:
*(technically not a Thoth but...)*
Takes eval-ables list as **states**. Each iteration, pops int **n** and executes **states[n]**. Stops if stack top is not a valid state index.

build_nested.d: Copy list #0 and set back to index #1

nested_modify.d: List iota #0 is the nested list to be modified. According to the index sequence given by list #1, traverses to the inner layer, and sets the corresponding element to iota #2.

mass_rotate.d: Accepts the size to reorder and a bottom-to-top order list, and do the corresponding reorder to the rest of the stack. For example, **3** plus **[1,2,0]** for Rotation Gambit, and **2** plus **[0,1,0,1]** for Dioscuri Gambit

weak_escape.d: Same as Consideration, but with lowest execution priority, and won't grow in **2^n** formula exponentially inside nested Intro-Retros

call_stack.d: Executes given pattern/list/Jump? iota in an independent stack, then recovers the original stack at bottom. If given an integer argument X no more than stack size, first X iotas will be taken away as the initial new stack.

wisp/summon/projectile.d: This wisp is summoned and launched like an arrow, casting its hex on whatever it hits. The initial stack when it executes will be a reference to itself, then a reference to what it hit.

wisp/summon/ticking.d: Similar to Summon Projectile Wisp, but with only one vector input for the position to summon the wisp. Cyclic wisps are unmoving once summoned, instead executing their hex up to 20 times each second.

wisp/self.d: Add a reference to the casting wisp to the stack. This must be cast by a wisp; trying to cast it through a staff will fail rather spectacularly.

wisp/media.d: Add the amount of media in the wisp's reservoir to the stack. This must be cast by a wisp; trying to cast it through a staff will fail rather spectacularly.

wisp/hex.d: Removes a reference to a wisp from the stack, and replaces it with the wisp's contained hex. Must be a wisp you summoned, or a wisp that has allowed transfer with the caster or caster's owner.

wisp/owner.d: Removes a reference to a wisp and an entity from the stack, and returns true if that entity owns that wisp, and false otherwise.

wisp/move/target/set.d: Removes a position vector from the stack; The Cyclic Wisp that executed this pattern will move in a straight line towards that position (colliding with terrain in its path) until it reaches it.

wisp/move/target/get.d: Adds to the stack the position vector that the executing Cyclic Wisp is currently moving towards.

wisp/move/speed/set.d: Removes a number from the stack, and sets the executing Cyclic Wisp's maximum speed to that number.

wisp/move/speed/get.d: Gets the executing Cyclic Wisp's current maximum speed.

wisp/transfer/allow.d: When two wisps are linked together, they transfer media between each other until they are balanced. By default this only happens between wisps with the same owner. This takes an index, and explicitly allows the wisp to exchange media with the linkable at that index.

wisp/transfer/disallow.d: Correspondingly, this takes an index and disallows the wisp from exchanging media with the linkable at that index.

wisp/transfer/others/allow.d: This takes a wisp that you own and an index, and allows the wisp to exchange media with the linkable at that index.

wisp/transfer/others/disallow.d: This takes a wisp that you own and an index, and disallows the wisp from exchanging media with the linkable at that index.

wisp/trigger/tick.d: Removes an integer from the stack, then delays the wisp's next cast until at least that many twentieth's of a second have passed. This and other triggers like it will halve the wisp's upkeep cost while it isn't casting.

wisp/trigger/comm.d: The wisp's next cast will not occur until it has received at least one communication.

wisp/trigger/move.d: The wisp's next cast will not occur until it has reached the position it is navigating towards.

wisp/seon/get.d: Returns my currently bound wisp. A new wisp can only be bound when this returns null. (This is not a great spell, I have simply placed it here for convenience.)

gate/mark.d: Consumes a gate iota and an entity. Marks that entity to be teleported the next time that gate is closed. Costs one twentieth of an Amethyst Dust.

gate/unmark.d: Consumes a gate iota and an entity. Unmarks that entity so that if it was marked with Gate's Opening it will no longer be teleported the next time that gate is closed.

gate/mark/get.d: Consumes a gate iota and an entity, returns whether that entity is marked by that gate.

wish.d: Wish the genie to cast a Hex for me. Because I am *teaching* a mind rather than *etching* a casting device, I can freely reteach the genie a new Hex any time without losing media.

true_eval.d: Casts a pattern or list of patterns like Hermes' Gambit if the next iota from the top of the stack is considered True by Nature.

false_eval.d: Casts a pattern or list of patterns like Hermes' Gambit if the next iota from the top of the stack is considered False by Nature.

main_for_each.d: Casts like Thoth's Gambit, however each sub-execution operates on the main stack instead of copies of the stack.

nulls/exec.d: If the first argument is not Null, returns it. Otherwise, executes the second argument, much like Hermes' Gambit.

reenable_minds.d: When I die, my embedded minds become unstable and cease to function. This spell restores them to working order. Costs one Amethyst Dust per mind restored.

make_jump_trigger.d: Creates a trigger that activates whenever I jump.
